videoTitle: Three Agents. One Doctor. Two Safe Retries. One Verified Release.
evidencePolicy: Every factual video claim maps to public repository evidence or the public Sepolia receipt. Offline fixtures are labeled and saved execution evidence is never presented as a live recording.

claims.claim: Claude Code, Codex, and Hermes each completed an authenticated read-only KeeperHub tool call.
Configured state is not treated as authenticated proof; the Doctor separately verifies an authenticated tools_documentation call.
Setup defaults to preview and prints official Agent-specific commands without applying them.
Doctor diagnostics use Step, Cause, Fix, and Evidence fields.
The onboarding teardown contains 11 ranked, reproducible blockers.
The frozen offline delivery gate records 115 of 115 automated tests passing.
An upstream-ready Quickstart documentation patch applies cleanly and has focused Go-test evidence.
KeeperHub supplies authenticated MCP, the organization wallet execution path, strict simulation, idempotent direct execution, and completion status for the demonstrated release.
The final release was bound to a satisfied file SHA-256 condition, a simulation and plan digest, and a real-TTY exact confirmation step.
The saved audit contains two retry events followed by one submit, one completed status, and one receipt; both retries use the same redacted idempotency digest.
The final KeeperHub release completed on Ethereum Sepolia with transaction hash 0xfcb18018db0969f984489332ee605f532acb052ce8a22b88880ef95147288975.
Because the receipt is EIP-7702, verification combines Success, decoded execute arguments, and state differences rather than equating outer relayer fields with the release intent.
Offline audit verification succeeds for 8 records with head 7781ff8fd7ab794777ae3d9189960d7e5825ff39db38f83fc02a3f0a3665ebaa.
